---
title: Versions
description: How an item's version counts its changes, so that two apps writing the same item never silently overwrite each other, and what Marfa does when they collide.
job: A builder learns why every write names a version and what happens when two apps write one item.
kind: concept

Many apps write to the same items, and a working copy may send a write made offline hours earlier. **A version on every item keeps that safe.**

## Optimistic concurrency

A write names the version it read, and Marfa checks what changed since before it applies anything. The `version` does the job an `ETag` and `If-Match` do in other HTTP APIs, but travels in the body or query, never in a header, and **a refused write answers `409 version_conflict`, not `412 Precondition Failed`.**

**By default a write can't overwrite a change it never saw;** `conflict=auto` lets the item type's merge policy settle a collision instead ([below](#let-marfa-settle-it)).

## What the version counts

An item's `version` starts at 1 and rises by one with each change to the item's own fields: its properties, type, **tier** (the library or the feed, [Items and types](/build/items-and-types#library-and-feed)), `occurred_at` or `source_id`. **Everything else leaves it alone:** tags, extensions, edges, rows, and moves between active, archived and the bin.

A write that would change nothing answers `200` with `acknowledged: true` and sends no event, so retrying a landed write is safe.

## When two apps write the same item

A write based on an older version isn't refused for that alone: Marfa compares the fields it changes with those changed since.

- **If they don't overlap, both changes stand,** and the item moves on.
- **If they overlap,** Marfa refuses the write with `409 version_conflict`. The answer names the `conflicting_fields` and carries the item as it is now (`current`) and as you read it (`ancestor`), so you can combine them.

You read a note at version 1, then another app changes its title and a third its body. Your new body collides on `body`.

<VersionOutcome />

Where a write depends on a field it reads and doesn't change, send `version_match: exact`: Marfa then refuses any write whose version isn't current, with no merge. [Update items without losing changes](/build/write-safely) shows both.

## Let Marfa settle it

A write sent with `conflict=auto` is settled by the **merge policy** of the item's type, field by field: `last_writer_wins`, or `keep_both_copies`. For a note's body, **both texts are kept:** the note keeps the body it holds, and yours goes into a **conflicted copy**, a new note with the original's tags plus `conflicted-copy`, linked to the original by a `derived-from` edge. A [working copy](/build/working-copies) sends every update this way.

## History

Each time the version moves, Marfa keeps a **snapshot** of the item as it was, with the **writer** of that version: the key, app or other sign-in that sent it. [List item versions](/reference/api/items/listItemVersions) reads them.

**Marfa keeps every recent snapshot and fewer as they age:** by default every one for 30 days, then one a day, then one a week, for a year in all, and never more than the newest 500 of one item. A write based on a version whose snapshot is gone is answered `409 ancestor_unavailable` with `current`, and the app reads the item again.

The rules behind this page are in the [versions](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/versions.md) chapter of the contract.
